correctness.rationale: For H triangle- and square-free, two horizontal neighbors in one layer of H×K2 occur together in exactly one closed-neighborhood generator; a second possible center would create a 3- or 4-cycle. The prescribed pairs indexed by at least two horizontal neighbors and optional vertical neighbor can therefore be removed in decreasing face cardinality, leaving exactly the union of tetrahedral boundaries on {v0,v1,w0,w1} over edges vw. Pair count is 4*sum(2^deg-deg-1), each sphere intersects a copy of H plus vertical edges along a contractible 3-edge path, and different spheres meet inside that base; this gives H∨m S2 integrally. Orienting each tetrahedral boundary yields unsigned edge-permutation H2 under automorphisms and +1 under layer switch. Oriented vertical squares generate the exact H1 kernel, with natural signed oriented-edge action and -1 under layer switch. Fresh independent Cech enumeration verified exact elementary free pairs and mod-two homology for K2, path4, cycle5; the finite results do not replace the universal uniqueness proof.
correctness.risk: The Čech model must be closed-ball radius-one nerve with graph edge interior metric, not the graph-square Vietoris–Rips complex.

final_claim: For connected finite triangle- and square-free H with n vertices and m edges, the scale-two Čech nerve of H×K2 collapses to the union of m tetrahedral boundaries, is homotopy equivalent to H∨m S2, and has H2 equal to the unsigned integral edge-permutation module; the scale-one-to-two H1 kernel is the signed oriented-edge module with negative layer-switch action.
limitations: H connected and finite; no triangles or four-cycles.
Finite-vertex graph Čech nerve with intrinsic unit-edge metric and closed radius-one balls, not graph Rips.
No equivariant ordering of elementary collapses is asserted.
